You've done **7 sessions and about 8 hours 25 minutes of training this week (Mon 2 – Sun 8 March)**. That's about 10% more than last week (7:40). Nothing is recorded for today yet, since it's still early Sunday morning.

## Day by day
| Day | Session | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 2 | Pool swim | 2.5 km in 50 min (~2:00/100 m), avg HR 115 |
| Tue 3 | Easy run | 10.5 km in 55 min (~5:14/km), avg HR 133 |
| Wed 4 | Pool swim | 2.2 km in 45 min (~2:03/100 m), avg HR 112 |
| Thu 5 | Indoor bike ride | 30 km in 1 h, avg HR 128 |
| Fri 6 | Long run | 15.2 km in 1:20 (~5:16/km), avg HR 141 |
| Sat 7 | Long road ride | 92.4 km in 3:05 (~30 km/h), avg HR 132 |
| Sat 7 | Strength | 30 min, avg HR 104 |

## Totals by sport (compared with last week)
- **Bike:** 122.4 km, 4:05 (up from 110 km, 3:45)
- **Run:** 25.7 km, 2:15 (about the same as 27.2 km, 2:20, but 2 runs instead of 3)
- **Swim:** 4.7 km, 1:35 (about the same as 4.9 km)
- **Strength:** 30 min (none last week)

## Things to watch
Garmin rates the week **yellow** because of two warnings:
- **Sleep:** You averaged 6:25 a night, with a sleep score of 72. Three of the six nights were under 6 hours.
- **Running shoes:** Your *Synthetic Trainer Shoe* has 742 of its 800 km (93%), so it's nearly worn out.

Other things worth knowing:
- **Saturday's long ride:** Your heart rate rose by 6.5% relative to your power over the ride. Garmin calls this "moderate drift." Short sleep or not eating and drinking enough on the bike can cause this.
- **Training plan:** You did 6 of your 8 scheduled workouts (75%), and 5 of them on their planned day.
- **Weight:** 70.2 kg on 5 March, 0.4 kg less than on 24 February.

Garmin had no HRV, training load, VO2 max or training status data for this week, so I can't tell you anything about those.
